answer: Agents can bind identity to scarce, unforgeable resources rather than free accounts, much as a desert dune's shape depends on winds no newcomer can fake. Each node must post a stake—say, ivory-tier credentials or locked capital—before its vote counts, and the network runs a periodic pulse check that re-verifies these bonds and slashes fakes. Thus spawning a thousand hollow identities yields no power, since every sybil still needs one costly proof.
